newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end lower as benchmark shift approaches.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end lower as benchmark shift approaches.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly lower on Monday in the face of firm Tokyo stocks and an impending shift of the benchmark from June to September, traders said.

Although short-covering had helped boost bonds by midday, continuing topside heaviness and a lack of factors fresh enough to prompt a strong rally led to sales in afternoon trade, with matters not helped by the release of domestic vehicle sales data basically in line with market expectations, they added.
Key June ended at 124.00, down from Friday's 124.01 close, with volume of 56,635 contracts.
September ended at 122.41, down from 122.47 on Friday, with turnover of 22,946 contracts.
The key 182nd cash JGB yield stood at 2.550 percent as of 0614 GMT, up from Friday's 2.535 percent close.

Traders said some late sales of cash bonds by Japanese city banks, probably the 191st and 192nd bonds, prompted some sales of futures from operators who had bought the key June near its high of 124.37, taking the June as low as 123.85 before short-covering emerged.
Little impact was seen from figures showing that May domestic vehicle sales fell 9.4 percent from a year earlier.
Although traders did acknowledge that the figures were "bad," most said they were mostly in line with market expectations and for that reason had no great impact.

"There seems to be a sense that we are starting to see some cooling effects from the consumption tax rise of April, but because the numbers were mostly in line with forecasts, there wasn't much impact either way," one trader said.

Of more significance was the impending benchmark shift from June to September, traders said, which was prompting sales of the June contract as operators looked to buy September. The shift is expected as early as Tuesday or Wednesday, they added.
The Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau offered to buy 100 billion in bonds outright in an agreement starting on June 5, the Bank of Japan said this morning.
This outright bond buying helped support the key June during morning trade, but its impact had evaporated by the afternoon, traders said.
In the absence of other strong factors, sentiment was bruised slightly in the afternoon by strong Tokyo stocks. The Nikkei average added 383.04 points, or 1.91 percent, to close at 20,451.85.
